status: station-based partner-agency witness, exploratory check, not the registered test
title: A second witness from the ground: station-based air temperature from KNMI Climate Explorer

witness.name: KNMI Climate Explorer (Royal Netherlands Meteorological Institute)
witness.dataset: CRU TS 4.10 mean temperature (tmp), 0.5 degree, land points, 1901-2025
witness.dataset_authors: Harris et al. 2020; University of East Anglia Climatic Research Unit (CRU)
witness.how_made: Climate Explorer 'Monthly observations' > Temperature (Land) > CRU TS 4.10 0.5 deg, 'Make average' over lat 60-70N, lon 165W-140W, land points only (more than 50 percent land from the CRU land/sea mask, at least 30 percent valid points), monthly series in degrees Celsius; annual mean computed here as the plain mean of the twelve monthly values
witness.citation: KNMI Climate Explorer, Royal Netherlands Meteorological Institute; data: CRU TS 4.10, Harris et al. 2020 / University of East Anglia CRU
witness.kind: station-based gridded analysis (weather stations interpolated to 0.5 degree), built from stations rather than satellite or model output

case.claim_text: Near-surface air temperature over interior and western Alaska has risen

levels.note: MERRA-2 level is the regional anomaly plus the registered baseline mean from the bundle (cos-latitude weights on cell anomalies, all cells in the box); CRU is land points only. Anomalies are each relative to their own 1981-2025 mean.

knmi_cru.sen_ci_method: analytic Sen interval (Gilbert) with Hamed-Rao variance, same routine as the registered test

our_merra2.sen_ci_method: analytic Sen interval (Gilbert) with Hamed-Rao variance, same routine as the registered test

difference_knmi_minus_merra2.sen_ci_method: analytic Sen interval (Gilbert) with Hamed-Rao variance, same routine as the registered test

registered_reference.note: Copied read-only from the registered case bundle. Nothing in this file changes it.
registered_reference.interval_method: analytic Sen interval (Gilbert) with Hamed-Rao variance

caveat: CRU TS is built from weather-station records, so it does not depend on satellites or on a reanalysis model, but it has its own limits: stations are sparse in interior and northern Alaska and their number has changed over time, so some grid cells lean on distant stations or on the long-term average. It covers land only and is an analysis of anomalies added to a climatology. Treat it as a cross-check on direction and year-to-year behaviour, not as ground truth.
scope_note: exploratory check, not the registered test. The registered result is the trend test in the case bundle; nothing here replaces it.
